quests.instruction: Read the text quickly and answer the question.
quests.passage: Books borrowed from the city library are due back after three weeks. If you keep a book longer, you pay ten cents for each extra day.
quests.question: What happens if a book is returned late?
options: The borrower loses the library card for a month
A fee is charged for every extra day
A fee is charged only once
quests.correctAnswer: A fee is charged for every extra day
quests.hint: Decide whether the penalty happens once or keeps growing.
quests.explanation: "Ten cents for each extra day" means the cost increases daily. The one-time fee is a tempting wrong answer if you read only the first half of the sentence.

quests.instruction: Read the text quickly and answer the question.
quests.passage: Your parcel was left with a neighbour at No. 14 because nobody was home when the courier came. You can collect it after five o'clock this evening.
quests.question: Where is the parcel now?
quests.hint: The text mentions a place where the parcel was NOT left and a place where it was. Keep them apart.
quests.explanation: The parcel is at No. 14 with a neighbour. The time in the second sentence tells you when it can be collected, not where it is.

quests.instruction: Read the text quickly and answer the question.
quests.passage: Ines joined a running group in April. At first she managed only five minutes without stopping, but after two months she could run for thirty.
quests.question: How did Ines's running change?
options: She now runs faster in every race she enters
She stopped running after two months
She could run much longer without stopping
quests.correctAnswer: She could run much longer without stopping
quests.hint: Compare the beginning and the end of the passage rather than one number.
quests.explanation: Five minutes grew to thirty minutes, so her endurance improved. Nothing says she raced or quit.

quests.instruction: Read the text quickly and answer the question.
quests.passage: The cinema now has cheaper tickets for morning shows before noon. Popcorn is not included, but every ticket comes with a free drink.
quests.question: What is included with every ticket?
options: A discount on the next visit
quests.hint: A negative statement and a positive one sit side by side here. Sort them out.
quests.explanation: Popcorn is explicitly not included, while the drink is. Watching for "not" prevents a common speed-reading mistake.

quests.instruction: Read the text quickly and answer the question.
quests.passage: The bank closes at 4:00 p.m. on weekdays, but the cash machine outside works all day and night. Deposits made after closing are processed the next working day.
quests.question: When will a deposit made at 6 p.m. on Tuesday be processed?
quests.hint: You need to combine the time of the deposit with the rule about closing.
quests.explanation: Six o'clock is after closing, so the deposit waits until the next working day, Wednesday. The passage gives the rule, and you apply it.

quests.instruction: Read the text quickly and answer the question.
quests.passage: Rosa waters her tomato plants early in the morning, before the sun is strong. She has learned that watering at midday makes the leaves burn.
quests.question: Why does Rosa water her plants early?
options: Midday water can damage the leaves
The plants grow faster at night
Tomatoes need less water in the sun
quests.correctAnswer: Midday water can damage the leaves
quests.hint: The reason follows a phrase about something Rosa discovered.
quests.explanation: Watering at midday burns the leaves, so she chooses an earlier time. "Damage" is a more general word for "burn."

quests.instruction: Read the text quickly and answer the question.
quests.passage: Glass, paper and plastic are collected on different days. Glass goes out on Tuesdays, paper on Thursdays, and plastic only every second Friday.
quests.question: Which material is collected least often?
quests.hint: Turn each collection day into a frequency before comparing.
quests.explanation: Glass and paper are weekly, while plastic is every two weeks. The word "only" is the clue that it is rarer.

quests.instruction: Read the text quickly and answer the question.
quests.passage: Sorry I missed your call, Jo. I was in a meeting until four. I'll ring you back on my way home, around half past five. Adrian
quests.question: When will Adrian probably call Jo?
quests.hint: Times are written in words here. Convert them before matching the options.
quests.explanation: "Half past five" is 5:30. Four o'clock is when his meeting ended, which is the detail that catches fast readers.

quests.instruction: Read the text quickly and answer the question.
quests.passage: The school lunch menu changes every week. This week, pasta is served on Monday and Wednesday, fish on Tuesday, and vegetable curry on Thursday and Friday.
quests.question: How many different main dishes are served this week?
quests.hint: Count the dishes, not the days.
quests.explanation: The dishes are pasta, fish and curry. Some appear on two days, so counting days would give five.

quests.instruction: Read the text quickly and answer the question.
quests.passage: Before you start the washing machine, check the pockets for coins or tissues. Then sort the clothes by colour, add the powder, and choose the temperature.
quests.question: What is the first step?
quests.hint: Order words such as "before" and "then" do the work in instructions.
quests.explanation: "Before you start" points to the pockets, and "then" introduces the rest. Sequence words save you from reading every step twice.

quests.instruction: Read the text quickly and answer the question.
quests.passage: Doors open at six, and the talk begins at half past six. After the talk there is a short break, and the questions start at eight.
quests.question: What happens between the talk and the questions?
quests.hint: Focus on the words that come right after the talk in the timeline.
quests.explanation: The talk is followed by a short break, then questions. The doors open earlier, before the talk.

quests.instruction: Read the text quickly and answer the question.
quests.passage: Tariq missed the 8:05 bus, so he walked to the next stop and caught the 8:20 instead. He reached the office at 8:50, ten minutes before his first meeting.
quests.question: When did Tariq's first meeting start?
quests.hint: The meeting time is never written as a clock time. Work it out from what is given.
quests.explanation: He arrived at 8:50, which was ten minutes before the meeting, so it started at 9:00. Three of the options are other times in the story.

quests.instruction: Read the text quickly and answer the question.
quests.passage: Building work on the second floor starts on Monday. Staff who normally sit there will move to the meeting rooms downstairs until the end of the month.
quests.question: Where will the second-floor staff work during the building work?
options: In an office in a different building
quests.hint: Ask where people sit normally, then where they go temporarily.
quests.explanation: The passage separates the usual place from the temporary one. "Until the end of the month" tells you the move is not permanent.

quests.instruction: Read the text quickly and answer the question.
quests.passage: The trail to the waterfall takes about two hours each way. Hikers should leave before noon so they are back before dark, and should carry plenty of water.
quests.question: Why should hikers leave before noon?
options: To avoid the crowds at the falls
To return before it gets dark
quests.correctAnswer: To return before it gets dark
quests.hint: A small linking word introduces the purpose of the advice.
quests.explanation: "So they are back before dark" gives the reason. Two hours each way means a late start could leave hikers walking in the dark.

quests.instruction: Read the text quickly and answer the question.
quests.passage: The store's new app shows which items are on sale near you. Users can also scan a product to check its price, and they get a coupon each time they shop.
quests.question: What can users do by scanning a product?
quests.hint: Keep each feature of the app separate; only one uses scanning.
quests.explanation: The scan feature is connected to checking a price. The sale list and the coupons are different features of the app.

quests.instruction: Read the text quickly and answer the question.
quests.passage: Hi everyone, the Friday meeting has moved from 10:00 to 2:00 because the manager will be at the airport in the morning. Please bring your weekly reports. Thanks, Helen
quests.question: Why has the meeting been moved?
options: The reports are still not finished
quests.hint: Find the reason before the request. Messages often give both in that order.
quests.explanation: The move is explained by the manager being at the airport, which the answer restates as travelling. "Please bring your weekly reports" is a separate instruction.

quests.instruction: Read the text quickly and answer the question.
quests.passage: This vacuum cleaner comes with a two-year guarantee. If it breaks in the first year, we repair or replace it free of charge. In the second year, you pay only for parts.
quests.question: What does the customer pay for in the second year?
quests.hint: The guarantee has two stages. Pay attention to which one the question asks about.
quests.explanation: Free repair or replacement applies in year one. In year two the customer covers the parts only, so "nothing" is wrong.

quests.instruction: Read the text quickly and answer the question.
quests.passage: Emma lost her wallet on the tram. A passenger found it and handed it to the driver, who called Emma that evening. Nothing was missing.
quests.question: Who contacted Emma?
quests.hint: Several people appear in this short text. Track what each one does.
quests.explanation: The passenger only found and handed in the wallet. The driver made the call, so "who called Emma" points to him.

quests.instruction: Read the text quickly and answer the question.
quests.passage: Students who want to join the drama club must sign up by Friday. Auditions will take place the following Tuesday, and the play itself will be performed in May.
quests.question: When are the auditions?
options: The Tuesday after the sign-up deadline
The Tuesday before the sign-up deadline
quests.correctAnswer: The Tuesday after the sign-up deadline
quests.hint: One word tells you how the audition day relates to the sign-up day.
quests.explanation: "The following Tuesday" means the Tuesday after Friday. May is the date of the performance, not the audition.

quests.instruction: Read the text quickly and answer the question.
quests.passage: Because of roadworks on Bridge Road, buses now use Mill Street. The trip takes about five minutes longer, and the stop outside the bank has moved to the corner.
quests.question: What has changed for bus passengers?
options: The trip is shorter but the fare is much higher
Bridge Road is closed to walkers
Journeys take longer and one stop has moved
Buses are more frequent and cheaper
quests.correctAnswer: Journeys take longer and one stop has moved
quests.hint: Two changes are described in the second sentence. Make sure your choice includes both.
quests.explanation: The extra five minutes and the moved bank stop are the two effects. The other options invent changes to fares or frequency.

quests.instruction: Read the text quickly and answer the question.
quests.passage: The local team lost its first three games but won the next four. Its coach says the players began to trust each other after a long talk in the locker room.
quests.question: What does the coach think caused the improvement?
quests.hint: Notice whose opinion this is. The explanation comes from one person in the text.
quests.explanation: The coach links the change to a talk that built trust. The other explanations are reasonable guesses, but none appear in the passage.

quests.instruction: Read the text quickly and answer the question.
quests.passage: Passengers on flight 218 should go to Gate 9 now. Boarding starts at 10:40, and anyone travelling with small children can board first. Hand luggage must fit in the overhead lockers.
quests.question: Who can board first?
options: Passengers who reached the gate earliest
quests.hint: In announcements, the group with special treatment is usually introduced by a phrase like "anyone who."
quests.explanation: Families with small children are allowed to board first. Gate 9 is where everyone gathers, not who gets priority.

quests.instruction: Read the text quickly and answer the question.
quests.passage: We can usually fix a cracked screen in one hour. If we need to order a part, the repair takes two or three days, and we will send you a message when your phone is ready.
quests.question: How will customers know their phone is ready?
options: It will be delivered to their door
The shop will send a message
quests.correctAnswer: The shop will send a message
quests.hint: The answer is a method of communication, mentioned at the end of the text.
quests.explanation: The shop promises a message once the repair is done. The one-hour and two-to-three-day times describe how long the repair takes, not how you are told.

quests.instruction: Read the text quickly and answer the question.
quests.passage: Bees are important for more than honey. As they move from flower to flower, they carry pollen, which helps many fruits and vegetables grow. Without bees, farmers would harvest much less food.
quests.question: Why are bees important to farmers?
options: They help crops produce fruit and vegetables
They protect crops from harmful insects and birds
quests.correctAnswer: They help crops produce fruit and vegetables
quests.hint: Connect what bees physically do with what happens to the plants.
quests.explanation: Carrying pollen helps fruit and vegetables grow, so farmers get more food. Honey is mentioned only to show that bees matter for other reasons too.

quests.instruction: Read the text quickly and answer the question.
quests.passage: Bright two-bedroom flat to rent near the station. The rent is nine hundred dollars a month, including water but not electricity. Pets are not allowed, and the flat is available from the first of June.
quests.question: What does the monthly rent include?
quests.hint: Watch the small words "including" and "not" in the same sentence.
quests.explanation: The rent covers water but not electricity. A reader who skims might connect "electricity" with the bills and choose it.

quests.instruction: Read the text quickly and answer the question.
quests.passage: The clinic offers free flu shots on Wednesday mornings for anyone over sixty-five. Younger adults can also get one, but they need to book an appointment and pay a small fee.
quests.question: Who can get a flu shot without paying?
quests.hint: Two groups are treated differently. Ask which one is described as free.
quests.explanation: Older adults get the shot free. Younger adults may also have one, but they book and pay, so the booking step does not make it free.

quests.instruction: Read the text quickly and answer the question.
quests.passage: Lucia used to drive to work, but traffic made her late twice a week. Now she takes the train, which costs slightly more but always arrives on time.
quests.question: Why does Lucia prefer the train?
quests.hint: Look at the advantage of the train, and remember what the passage says about its cost.
quests.explanation: "Always arrives on time" means dependable. The train costs slightly more, so "cheaper" is the opposite of what the text says.

quests.instruction: Read the text quickly and answer the question.
quests.passage: The community garden needs volunteers on Saturday mornings. Beginners are welcome and tools are provided, but please wear old clothes and bring a water bottle. In return, volunteers can take home some of the vegetables.
quests.question: What do volunteers receive?
quests.hint: A phrase near the end shows what volunteers get in exchange for their time.
quests.explanation: "In return" introduces the reward. Tools and bottles are things mentioned earlier, but volunteers use or bring them; they do not receive them.

quests.instruction: Read the text quickly and answer the question.
quests.passage: If your flight is cancelled, contact the airline first, not the airport. The airline can rebook you on the next available flight and may offer a hotel if the delay is long. Keep all your receipts.
quests.question: What is the airline's job when a flight is cancelled?
quests.hint: Ask what the passenger needs after a cancellation, and which organisation provides it.
quests.explanation: "Rebook you on the next flight" is the airline's main role. The last sentence advises the passenger to keep receipts; it does not say the airline collects them.

quests.instruction: Read the text quickly and answer the question.
quests.passage: Many people believe they need eight glasses of water a day. In fact, the amount depends on the weather, exercise and body size, and foods such as fruit and soup also provide water.
quests.question: What does the passage conclude about how much water people need?
options: Exercise is dangerous in very hot weather
Water needs differ from person to person
quests.correctAnswer: Water needs differ from person to person
quests.hint: A phrase in the second sentence signals that the passage will challenge the first idea.
quests.explanation: The passage sets up a common belief and then corrects it. Recognising that shift is the key to finding the main idea quickly.
